proof_nl:
Let H_m := \sum_{j=1}^m \frac1j. Fix an integer n>1 and a real x with \frac{n-1}{n} \le x < 1.

For each k with 1 \le k \le n-1, we have
kx \ge k\cdot \frac{n-1}{n} = k - \frac{k}{n} > k-1,
because k<n implies \frac{k}{n}<1. Also kx<k since x<1. Hence k-1 < kx < k, so \lfloor kx\rfloor = k-1.
For k=n, we get n-1 \le nx < n, so \lfloor nx\rfloor = n-1.

Therefore
E(n,x)= (n-1)-\sum_{k=1}^{n-1}\frac{k-1}{k}-\frac{n-1}{n}.
Now \frac{k-1}{k}=1-\frac1k, so
\sum_{k=1}^{n-1}\frac{k-1}{k} = (n-1)-\sum_{k=1}^{n-1}\frac1k = (n-1)-H_{n-1}.
Substituting,
E(n,x)= (n-1)-\bigl((n-1)-H_{n-1}\bigr)-\frac{n-1}{n} = H_{n-1}-\frac{n-1}{n}.
Since H_n = H_{n-1}+\frac1n, this equals
H_n-1.
Thus E(n,x)=H_n-1 for every x in \left[\frac{n-1}{n},1\right).
solver_summary: On the interval [(n-1)/n,1), one has floor(kx)=k-1 for k<n and floor(nx)=n-1. Substituting into E(n,x) and simplifying via the harmonic numbers gives the constant value H_n-1.
